src/core/world.cpp.local_changes: Optional validated WorldConfig scales body radii, terrain amplitudes, atmosphere and orbital distances together, preserving default constructor output and original gravity/orbit periods. Geography-scale sampling retains proportional color and normal thresholds. Temperate ground uses continuous moisture, elevation and temperature transitions for grass, rock, snow and coast colors.

src/core/terrain.cpp.local_changes: One shared planner offers explicit selected-body planning with existing screen-error/balance-closure priority; legacy all-world order/signature are preserved. Optional world size scales geometric normal stencils, minimum skirts and geographic vegetation eligibility without adding a second mesher. An additive explicit ocean-surface planner overload scores the closest rendered ground or sea surface only for admitted wet requests; original terrain-only overloads, mesh generation, gravity and landing samples remain unchanged. Optional validated TerrainView adds a conservative full-height patch envelope and an explicit in-view queue tier while retaining complete balanced coarse coverage and unchanged no-view ordering; it is detail priority, not renderer occlusion. A bounded double-precision procedural camera-ray march prioritizes its actual visible-surface hit, with a derived height-field Lipschitz bound, 5cm target tolerance, a bounded 16384-step budget for grazing rays, and conservative no-hit/exhaustion fallback. The ray-hit ancestry receives at most two extra detail levels under the same maximum level, balanced coverage and fixed leaf budget. This is refinement only, not a collision query. An optional camera-up field enables forward, exactly 45-degree camera-down with roll, and radial-nadir refinement rays near the visible ground or sea surface. Each ray retains its 16384-step limit (49152 aggregate per selected body). A cubic smooth altitude weight trades the three-hit attention for a broad viewport region with a smooth outer taper; the queue combines continuous attention and bounded monotonic screen-error priority, retaining the existing at-most-two-level screen-error bias. Near bound is clamp(radius*0.002,25m,5000m); far is max(near*4,clamp(radius*0.02,250m,100000m)). At or above far no focus rays run and off-screen nadir/down branches receive no special refinement. Legacy no-up ordering and scores, fixed leaf and memory budgets, maximum level and complete 2:1-balanced coverage remain unchanged. Temperate terrain mesh color blends exposed rock using its LOD-invariant vertex normal and body-space tint field. Camera-ray interval and patch-priority planning now call the shared terrain relief bound, with the same coefficients and evaluation order. Seeded metric-scale albedo variation adds resolved contrast to flatter temperate ground while preserving the existing geometry, steep-rock blend and shoreline colors. Low-altitude camera-up views also score a tapered body-radial ground disk independently of yaw and roll. It intersects conservative tile bounds and spreads refinement around the observer before spending remaining budget on the finest local patches. The existing focus rays, complete balanced cut, maximum level, cache residency and hard leaf budget remain authoritative. A smoothly tapered forward ground footprint extends low-altitude near-horizontal flight detail within the existing leaf budget and leaves the camera and coverage constraints unchanged. Share the unchanged mesh anchor and radial skirt arithmetic with the package's exact undeformed water lattice provider, including retained wet parents and dry endpoints.

Use the shared named 1.8 m collision and camera clearance in the original movement and contact calculations.

boundary: One retained upstream ABI/algorithm owner with adapted camera-priority and optional physical-size contracts. Facades are not a completed implementation-module conversion. Original application, renderer, platform loops and worker pool remain excluded. Engine host owns scheduling, memory admission, package approval and camera/render mapping. Default producer mesh/JSON/cache/stream and exploration-session versions remain unchanged; custom size uses typed versioned receipts and immutable cache identity. The additive terrain.frame file reports exact export scale/origin/key/counts without changing the mesh codec. These CPU libraries and input bounds do not prove native ground fidelity, smooth geomorph or large-world editing.
